title: THE STORM THAT SHOOK A NATION

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand towards the sky so that hail will fall all over Egypt—on people and animals and on everything growing in the fields of Egypt." When Moses stretched out his staff towards the sky, the Lord sent thunder and hail, and lightning flashed down to the ground. So the Lord rained hail on the land of Egypt; hail fell and lightning flashed back and forth. It was the worst storm in all the land of Egypt since it had become a nation." - Exodus 9:22-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Egypt was a land where rain was rare and storms rarer still. Their whole civilisation depended on the predictable rising of the Nile, not on weather from the sky. This was outside anything they knew how to manage.

God often works exactly there — beyond the range of our systems and contingency plans.

Egypt worshipped the sky and the storm among its gods. Now the sky itself turns against the nation that worshipped it. What people put in God's place will not protect them.

But notice Moses' part in all this. He stretches out his hand. That is all. The thunder, the lightning, the hail — none of that came from Moses. He simply obeyed the small instruction, and God did the rest.

Whatever storm you are facing, remember who commands the weather. The disciples once asked in terror, who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him (Mk 4:41). We know the answer to their question.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What situation feels completely outside my control right now?
2. Do I believe the One who commands storms is also in my boat?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You rule the skies and the storms. Steady me in what I cannot control and keep my eyes on You. Amen.
